entries.title: nish/crypto/bcrypt-batch, a login batcher across cores
entries.body:
bcryptBatcher(config) queues verify and hash requests and sends a batch
at bcryptCalibrate()'s width, or once the oldest request has waited a
configurable hold (0 sends at once). run() splits the queue into one
share per core, runs each share on a std/threads task with
bcryptVerifyN/bcryptHashN, and answers by ticket. A one-core full batch
costs 15.7 ms a hash against 56.9 for a lone one, which is what filling
batches buys.

Each queued password is a copy held as a Secret and wiped in run() once
the scope joins; what crosses the tasks is the answer text, nothing
secret. A damaged hash in a batch falls back to lone verifies so one bad
row answers alone; a bad salt is refused at hash() and never queued. A
batcher dropped with requests still queued leaves those copies unwiped
(BCRYPT-11, Low, accepted; call run() until pending() is 0).

On four cores the batcher answers 1.9 to 2.3 times the logins a second
of one bcryptVerify per login per core from 120 arrivals a second up.
At 10 to 60 arrivals a second it loses to that server on latency,
because run() blocks the dispatcher until every share is done; the
record and the guide say so.
metrics: cost 10, 4-vCPU Xeon @ 2.80GHz, 5 rounds, noise band <=1% logins/s, <=11% p50, <=10% p99 (byte-identical twin)
1 core, burst: 46.0 logins/s vs 16.9 one-per-login; 30/s: 31.7 vs 16.9
